categories.name: Economic
categories.title: 📈 Economic, Per Capita Wealth & Capital Markets Atlas
categories.description: Macroeconomic balance sheet, per capita Net National Income (₹2.18 Lakh), purchasing power parity (PPP), monetary policy, GDP growth trajectory, trade openness, Union Budget fiscal balance, and global equity market comparisons.

subgroups.name: Macroeconomics
subgroups.title: 📊 Macroeconomics & Growth Trajectory
subgroups.description: Core macroeconomic balance sheet: GDP per capita, CPI inflation, Union fiscal deficit, current account balance, tax-to-GDP ratio, and gross domestic savings.

subgroups.name: Per Capita Income & Wealth
subgroups.title: 💰 Per Capita Income & National Wealth Trajectory
subgroups.description: India's per capita Net National Income (NNI) growth in Indian Rupees (₹2.18 Lakh) alongside GNI per capita in Purchasing Power Parity (PPP current international $).

subgroups.name: Manufacturing & Industrial Growth
subgroups.title: 🏭 Manufacturing Sectors & Industrial Performance
subgroups.description: Industrial growth engines boosted by Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes: General IIP index, Eight Core Industries index, automobile production volume (SIAM), crude steel output (2nd largest globally), electronics & smartphone manufacturing value (MeitY), pharma exports (Pharmexcil), and textiles/apparel export trajectory.

subgroups.name: Trade & External
subgroups.title: 🌐 External Trade & Foreign Reserves
subgroups.description: Trade openness ratio, foreign exchange reserves (forex), official rupee-dollar exchange rate, and monthly merchandise export/import bills.

subgroups.name: Monetary Policy
subgroups.title: 🏛️ Monetary Policy & Banking Credit
subgroups.description: Financial system liquidity, money supply (M3 broad money share of GDP), and private sector bank credit expansion.

subgroups.name: Production & Commodities
subgroups.title: 🛢️ Commodities, Energy & High-Frequency Signals
subgroups.description: Indian crude oil basket pricing, petroleum fuel product consumption, WPI wholesale price inflation, and high-frequency production indicators.

subgroups.name: Media & Publications
subgroups.title: 📰 Media & Public Data Cadence
subgroups.description: Transparent public-data publication signals and Substack writing cadence.

subgroups.name: Markets
subgroups.title: 📈 Capital Markets & Global Benchmarks
subgroups.description: BSE Sensex, Nifty 50, and Nifty VIX rebased to 100 alongside benchmark comparisons with US S&P 500, UK FTSE 100, Japan Nikkei 225, China Shanghai Composite, and top global GDP economies.

subgroups.name: Fiscal & Union Budget
subgroups.title: 📜 Union Budget & Fiscal Expansion
subgroups.description: Post-independence Union Budget expenditure trajectory (₹48.2 Lakh Cr), annual expenditure YoY growth %, strategic Capex allocation for capital asset creation, and gross central tax revenue buoyancy.

categories.name: Industry Trends & Performance
categories.title: 🏭 Industry Trends, Performance & Industrial Stability Atlas
categories.description: Manufacturing expansion, PLI scheme impact, automobile production, crude steel, electronics, pharmaceuticals, textiles, 100% railway electrification, National Highways construction, clean energy capacity, and core industrial indices.

subgroups.name: Production & Commodities
subgroups.title: 🛢️ Commodities, Energy & High-Frequency Signals
subgroups.description: Indian crude oil basket pricing, petroleum fuel product consumption, WPI wholesale price inflation, and high-frequency production indicators.

subgroups.name: Infrastructure Development
subgroups.title: 🛣️ Infrastructure Development & Connectivity Networks
subgroups.description: Physical and digital asset creation: National Highways construction cadence (km/yr), 100% Railway electrification share, renewable power capacity (GW), civil aviation passenger traffic, power consumption, e-way bills, rail freight, port cargo, and high-speed broadband expansion.

subgroups.name: Manufacturing & Industrial Growth
subgroups.title: 🏭 Manufacturing Sectors & Industrial Performance
subgroups.description: Industrial growth engines boosted by Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes: General IIP index, Eight Core Industries index, automobile production volume (SIAM), crude steel output (2nd largest globally), electronics & smartphone manufacturing value (MeitY), pharma exports (Pharmexcil), and textiles/apparel export trajectory.

subgroups.name: Food Processing & Consumer Goods
subgroups.title: 🍚 Food Processing & Consumer Manufacturing
subgroups.description: Food products, beverages, tobacco, textiles, apparel, leather, wood, paper, printing and furniture: the labour-intensive consumer industries, with UNIDO's composition of manufacturing value added.

subgroups.name: Heavy Industry & Metals
subgroups.title: 🏗️ Heavy Industry, Metals & Capital Goods
subgroups.description: Basic metals (iron, steel, aluminium), fabricated metal products, machinery, electrical equipment, cement and other non-metallic minerals, and refined petroleum, tracked through MOSPI's Index of Industrial Production since 2011-12, plus UNIDO's technology-intensity split.

subgroups.name: Automobiles & Transport Equipment
subgroups.title: 🚗 Cars, Two-Wheelers & Transport Equipment
subgroups.description: Output of motor vehicles (cars, utility vehicles, trucks, trailers) and other transport equipment (dominated by two-wheelers), monthly and annual from MOSPI IIP, with SIAM's segment-wise production mix.

subgroups.name: Chemicals, Pharma & Electronics
subgroups.title: 💊 Chemicals, Pharmaceuticals & Electronics
subgroups.description: Chemicals, pharmaceuticals, rubber and plastics, and computers, electronics and optical products: India's process and high-technology manufacturing base.

subgroups.name: Industrial Output Monitor (IIP)
subgroups.title: 📡 Industrial Output Monitor
subgroups.description: Monthly IIP by use (capital, intermediate, infrastructure, consumer durables and non-durables), industry growth rankings, cumulative change since 2011-12, and how many industries are expanding versus contracting.

categories.name: Mining & Natural Resources
categories.title: ⛏️ Mined Resources, Minerals & Energy Commodities Atlas
categories.description: India's mineral wealth and strategic resource security: metallic ores (iron ore, bauxite, copper, manganese), energy minerals (coal, lignite, domestic crude, natural gas), industrial minerals (limestone, rare earths), and mineral export trade.

subgroups.name: Metallic Minerals & Ores
subgroups.title: ⛏️ Metallic Minerals & Ferrous/Non-Ferrous Ores
subgroups.description: Foundational metallic mineral production powering heavy industry: Iron Ore output (315 MT), Bauxite for aluminium smelting (27.8 MT), Refined Copper output (615k Tonnes), and Manganese Ore (38.2 Lakh Tonnes).

subgroups.name: Energy Minerals & Fuel
subgroups.title: 🔥 Energy Minerals & Fossil Fuel Resources
subgroups.description: Baseload power and domestic fuel production: total domestic Coal production (1.14 Billion Tonnes), Lignite brown coal mining (54.8 MT), domestic Crude Petroleum output (30.8 MMT), and offshore/onshore Natural Gas production (42 BCM).

subgroups.name: Non-Metallic & Industrial Minerals
subgroups.title: 🧱 Non-Metallic, Industrial & Critical Minerals
subgroups.description: Raw materials for construction, fertilizers, and technology: Limestone production for cement (505 MT), IREL Critical Minerals & Rare Earth Elements (REE) Index, and Rock Phosphate/Gypsum for chemical fertilizers.

subgroups.name: Mineral Exports & Trade
subgroups.title: 🚢 Mineral & Metal Exports & Strategic Trade Reliance
subgroups.description: Global mineral trade trajectory: total Mineral & Metal export value ($38.5 Billion), Iron Ore export volume (49.5 MT), Refined Petroleum product export volume (71.5 MMT), and Critical Mineral Strategic Import Dependency Index (reduced from 100% to 68.5%).

subgroups.name: Mining Output Monitor (IIP)
subgroups.title: ⛏️ Mining Output Monitor
subgroups.description: Annual and monthly mining and quarrying output from MOSPI's Index of Industrial Production, compared with manufacturing and electricity, with growth trends and mining's official weight in the IIP.

subgroups.name: Mineral Price Monitor (WPI)
subgroups.title: 💹 Mineral Price Monitor
subgroups.description: Official monthly wholesale prices of iron ore, bauxite, copper, zinc, lead, manganese, chromite, limestone, rock phosphate, crude oil, natural gas, coal and lignite since 2012, with inflation rankings, price-change bands and rising-vs-falling pies.

categories.name: Payments & Digital Banking
categories.title: 💳 Payments & Digital Financial Infrastructure Atlas
categories.description: The world's largest real-time retail payment transformation: UPI transaction volume and annual value (₹265 Lakh Cr), credit & debit card POS spends, active card circulation, and official RBI Digital Payments Index (DPI).

subgroups.name: UPI & Digital Payments
subgroups.title: ⚡ UPI & Real-Time Digital Payments
subgroups.description: The world's leading real-time payment system: monthly UPI transaction volume and annual transaction value (₹265 Lakh Crores).

subgroups.name: Card Spends & Ecosystem
subgroups.title: 💳 Credit & Debit Card Ecosystem
subgroups.description: Annual consumer spending on credit cards (₹25.8 Lakh Cr) vs debit card POS transactions (₹6.8 Lakh Cr) and active card circulation counts (12.8 Cr Credit, 101.5 Cr Debit).

subgroups.name: Digital Financial Index
subgroups.title: 📊 RBI Digital Payments Index (RBI DPI)
subgroups.description: Official Reserve Bank of India composite index measuring digital payment enablement, infrastructure, performance, and consumer centricity across India (Base 100 = March 2018).

categories.name: State Performance & Regional Health
categories.title: 🏛️ State Performance, GSDP & Regional Industrial Health
categories.description: State-wise economic, financial, and welfare comparison across India's federal landscape: GSDP growth trajectories, operating factory counts, fiscal deficit and own-tax ratios to GSDP, PMAY housing completions, Jal Jeevan tap water coverage, and PM MUDRA loan disbursements.

subgroups.name: State Financial Health & GSDP
subgroups.title: 🏛️ State Financial Health & GSDP Growth
subgroups.description: GSDP trajectories comparing India's largest state economies (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka, UP, West Bengal) alongside RBI fiscal-deficit and own-tax-revenue ratios to GSDP.

subgroups.name: State Welfare & Scheme Coverage
subgroups.title: 🏡 State Welfare Scheme Execution
subgroups.description: State-level delivery of national welfare infrastructure: PMAY pucca housing units built, Jal Jeevan Mission Har Ghar Jal tap water access %, and PM MUDRA micro-credit loan disbursements.

subgroups.name: State Industrial & Manufacturing Hubs
subgroups.title: 🏭 State Manufacturing & Investment Hubs
subgroups.description: State export-preparedness and ease-of-doing-business snapshots, alongside RBI factory-employment rankings.

categories.name: Public Health & Epidemiology
categories.title: 🩺 Public Health, Lifespan Milestones & Epidemiology Atlas
categories.description: National health indicators from World Bank/WHO and the RBI state handbook: infant, under-five and maternal mortality, tuberculosis and malaria incidence, causes of death, health spending and who pays for care, plus State/UT health outcomes.

subgroups.name: Health Infrastructure & Spending
subgroups.title: 🏥 Government Health Spending & Out-of-Pocket Expenditure
subgroups.description: Health financing from WHO Global Health Expenditure data: current and government health spending, out-of-pocket share, hospital beds, physicians, immunisation and water and sanitation access.

subgroups.name: Mortality & Lifespan Milestones
subgroups.title: 👶 Infant & Maternal Mortality Milestones
subgroups.description: World Bank infant, neonatal and under-five mortality (per 1,000 live births) and the modelled maternal mortality ratio (per 100,000 live births).

subgroups.name: Disease Burden & Epidemiology
subgroups.title: 🔬 Disease Burden & Epidemiological Transition
subgroups.description: Shifting epidemiology: WHO tuberculosis and malaria incidence, smoking prevalence, and the World Bank causes-of-death split between communicable, non-communicable and injury deaths.

subgroups.name: Nutrition & Food Security
subgroups.title: 🍲 Nutrition & Food Security
subgroups.description: FAO undernourishment estimates and modelled child-stunting rates, the outcomes targeted by the National Food Security Act and POSHAN Abhiyaan.

categories.name: Social
categories.title: 👥 Demographics, Welfare & Human Capital
categories.description: Long-term social transformation across decades: 1.4B population dynamics, nationwide electrification, high-speed broadband access, flagship welfare schemes, and life expectancy milestones.

subgroups.name: Demographics
subgroups.title: 👥 Demographics & Social Equity
subgroups.description: Total 1.4B population trajectory, labour force unemployment rate, literacy rate breakdowns across SC/ST/OBC social categories, religious community literacy rates, and PM MUDRA loan social inclusion distribution.

subgroups.name: Welfare
subgroups.title: 🏥 Social Welfare & Essential Access
subgroups.description: Universal household electricity access (100%), internet penetration %, and life expectancy at birth milestones.

subgroups.name: Gender & Population
subgroups.title: ⚖️ Gender & Population
subgroups.description: Sample Registration System sex ratio at birth, Census sex ratio since 1951, women's age at marriage, fertility by women's education and women in Parliament.

subgroups.name: Higher Education
subgroups.title: 🎓 Universities, Colleges & Research
subgroups.description: AISHE counts of universities and colleges, enrolment by sex, level and social group, State-wise GER, and World Bank R&D spending and researcher density.

categories.name: Environment & Climate
categories.title: 🌿 Environment, Climate & Energy Transition
categories.description: Official Government of India environment statistics from MoSPI's EnviStats India: IMD temperature, rainfall and cyclone records, Forest Survey of India forest cover, CPCB waste data, NCRB deaths from natural causes and CEA electricity generation by source, plus World Bank emissions, water and protected-area indicators. Every chart explains what it shows, how to read it and why it matters.
badges: MoSPI EnviStats · IMD · FSI · CPCB · CEA

subgroups.name: Climate & Weather
subgroups.title: 🌦️ Temperature, Rainfall, Cyclones & Heat
subgroups.description: IMD's all-India seasonal temperature since 2001, annual and monsoon rainfall, cyclonic storms over the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea, State heat-wave days, and World Bank CO2 and greenhouse-gas emissions.

subgroups.name: Forests & Land
subgroups.title: 🌳 Forests, Water & Land
subgroups.description: Forest cover from every State of Forest Report since 2001, nationally and by State, with protected areas, renewable freshwater per person and population density.

subgroups.name: Pollution & Waste
subgroups.title: ♻️ Urban Waste & Plastic
subgroups.description: Municipal solid waste generated, collected, treated and landfilled by State, and national plastic-waste estimates from the Central Pollution Control Board.

subgroups.name: Disasters & Extremes
subgroups.title: ⛈️ Disasters & Deaths from Natural Causes
subgroups.description: NCRB counts of deaths from lightning, floods, heat stroke, cold, landslides and cyclones: the human cost of weather extremes.

subgroups.name: Energy Transition
subgroups.title: ⚡ Electricity Generation & the Energy Transition
subgroups.description: Central Electricity Authority generation since 1947 by source (coal, gas, hydro, nuclear, renewables) and the latest generation mix.

categories.name: Agriculture & Food
categories.title: 🌾 Agriculture, Food & Farm Inputs
categories.description: Foodgrain, oilseed and sugarcane production from the Ministry of Agriculture, fertiliser use and imports from the Department of Fertilizers, the Livestock Census and fish production, all through MoSPI's API, alongside World Bank irrigation, fertiliser-intensity and food-production indices.

subgroups.name: Farm Inputs
subgroups.title: 🚜 Fertiliser, Irrigation & Land
subgroups.description: N-P-K fertiliser consumption, production and imports since 1981-82, fertiliser intensity per hectare, irrigated share and arable land per person.

subgroups.name: Crop Production
subgroups.title: 🌾 Foodgrains, Oilseeds & Sugarcane
subgroups.description: Crop-year production of rice, wheat, coarse cereals, pulses, oilseeds and sugarcane, with the World Bank food production index.

subgroups.name: Livestock & Fisheries
subgroups.title: 🐄 Livestock & Fisheries
subgroups.description: Livestock Census counts of cattle, buffaloes, goats, sheep and pigs since 1951, and inland vs marine fish production since 1950-51.

categories.name: Defence & Strategic
categories.title: 🛡️ Defence, Arms Production & Strategic Modernization Atlas
categories.description: India's defense manufacturing evolution, historic Make in India defense export surge (₹23,497 Cr), indigenous production (₹1.45 Lakh Cr), SIPRI arms capability trends, DRDO R&D, and defense capital acquisition modernization.

subgroups.name: Defence Budget & Modernization
subgroups.title: 🎖️ Defence Allocation & R&D Capital Outlay
subgroups.description: Defence expenditure share of Union Budget, DRDO R&D research allocation, and Capital Acquisition Outlay for modernizing weapons, aircraft, naval frigates, and artillery.

subgroups.name: Defence Exports & Production
subgroups.title: 🚀 Defence Manufacturing & Export Engine
subgroups.description: Indigenous defence production surge (₹1.45 Lakh Cr) across DPSUs and private sector enterprises, alongside historic Make in India defence export growth (₹23,497 Cr to 85+ nations).

subgroups.name: Strategic Stockpiles & Capabilities
subgroups.title: 🛡️ Strategic Stockpiles & Arms Imports Trend
subgroups.description: SIPRI arms inventory & conventional capability index, alongside declining foreign arms import reliance as indigenous defence manufacturing expands.

categories.name: Crime & Security
categories.title: ⚖️ Public Safety, Internal Security & Anti-Insurgency Atlas
categories.description: Comprehensive national security atlas: Left-Wing Extremism (LWE / Maoism) 22-year fatality decline, Jammu & Kashmir terrorism reduction (2000-2025), North East insurgency pacification (2000-2025), historical Punjab militancy archive (1981-1995), NDPS drug offences, child protection/POCSO cases, road accident fatalities, and police strength.

subgroups.name: North East Insurgency
subgroups.title: 🌲 North East Insurgency Pacification
subgroups.description: Decadal decline in insurgent fatalities and registered incidents across North Eastern states following peace accords and border security operations.

subgroups.name: Jammu & Kashmir Insurgency
subgroups.title: 🏔️ Jammu & Kashmir Counter-Terrorism & Insurgency
subgroups.description: Annual counter-terrorism fatalities and terrorist incident volume in J&K showing a steep structural decline in violence levels.

subgroups.name: Punjab Militancy & Security
subgroups.title: 🌾 Historical Punjab Militancy & Security Archive
subgroups.description: Historical fatality archive tracking the Punjab militancy period (1981-1995) prior to the restoration of full peace and democratic stability.

subgroups.name: Violence & Crime
subgroups.title: ⚖️ Cognizable Crime & Public Safety
subgroups.description: Historical IPC cognizable crime rates per 100k (1951-2023), NCRB 2023 crime category snapshot, crimes against women rate, cyber crime case volume, economic offences rate, NDPS drug offences, child protection/POCSO cases, road accident fatalities, and police strength.

subgroups.name: Maoism / LWE
subgroups.title: ⛰️ Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) & Maoist Insurgency
subgroups.description: Ministry of Home Affairs official LWE aggregate fatalities (8,956 killed 2004-2025) alongside annual LWE deaths trajectory (2004-2025) and South Asia Terrorism Portal (SATP 2000-2025) annual casualty breakdown across Civilians, Security Forces, and Perpetrators.

subgroups.name: Terrorism
subgroups.title: 💥 Counter-Terrorism & Event Trends
subgroups.description: Global Terrorism Database (GTD) open series tracking terrorist attack counts and human fatalities in India (1970-2020).

categories.name: Pew Research
categories.title: 📊 Global Standing & Public Opinion
categories.description: Pew Research Center global attitudes studies tracking international perception, economic confidence, bilateral ties, and leadership opinions.

subgroups.name: Public opinion
subgroups.title: 📊 Pew Research Public Opinion & Global Attitudes
subgroups.description: Landmark Pew Research Center survey snapshots: global power perceptions, US-India bilateral ties, domestic economic confidence, religious tolerance & pluralism (29,999 respondents), gender equality views, news media trust, and climate change awareness.

categories.name: Elections
categories.title: 🗳️ Election Results Atlas
categories.description: Explore current ECI candidate results alongside a growing archive of downloadable ECI historical statistical reports. Historical rows are source-linked and selectable by election, state and constituency; available archived workbooks do not yet provide complete coverage of every election year or state.

subgroups.name: Indian Elections
subgroups.title: 🗳️ Indian Lok Sabha & State Assembly Results
subgroups.description: Compare currently published ECI constituency tables with candidate rows parsed from available ECI historical statistical-report workbooks. Select an available election, year, State/UT and constituency to inspect the original reported votes. The historical workbook archive is partial: missing periods or seats are unavailable, not zero, and live results remain provisional until Form 20.

categories.name: U.S. Elections
categories.title: 🇺🇸 U.S. Elections & Campaign Finance
categories.description: Explore U.S. presidential Electoral College outcomes from the National Archives alongside Federal Election Commission candidate-finance summaries for presidential, Senate and House cycles. Finance charts report aggregate receipts, disbursements, cash on hand and debts by party or candidate office state; they are not voting or turnout measures.

subgroups.name: U.S. Presidential Elections
subgroups.title: 🇺🇸 U.S. Presidential Elections
subgroups.description: Compare completed U.S. Presidential Electoral College results from the National Archives. Electoral College totals are not popular votes or ballots cast; campaign finances are presented in separate subgroups.

subgroups.name: U.S. Presidential Campaign Finance
subgroups.title: 💵 U.S. Presidential Campaign Finance
subgroups.description: Compare Federal Election Commission candidate receipts, disbursements, cash on hand and debts by party across presidential-office campaign-finance cycles. These filing-cycle snapshots are financial aggregates, not electoral results; some cycle years are midterms with no Presidential election.

subgroups.name: U.S. Congressional Campaign Finance
subgroups.title: 🏛️ U.S. Congressional Campaign Finance
subgroups.description: Compare FEC-reported House and Senate candidate receipts, disbursements, cash on hand and debts by candidate office state. These are campaign-finance totals—not votes, turnout, or winning seats.

categories.name: Tourism & Heritage
categories.title: 🏛️ Tourism & UNESCO World Heritage
categories.description: Follow annual international visitor and receipts indicators, then explore India’s UNESCO World Heritage properties by inscription year. Visitor totals are national, while the heritage series is reconstructed from current official inscription records; neither is a state-wise monument attendance measure.

subgroups.name: International Visitor Trends
subgroups.title: 🧳 International Visitor Trends
subgroups.description: Track World Bank annual counts of international arrivals and departures alongside international tourism receipts in current US dollars. These are national measures reported at different frequencies of availability; receipts are nominal, and the indicators do not measure domestic travel, visits to individual monuments or State-level tourism.

subgroups.name: World Heritage Sites
subgroups.title: 🏛️ UNESCO World Heritage Inscription Record
subgroups.description: Explore annual inscription events, a cumulative count reconstructed from current UNESCO property pages, and current cultural/natural/mixed classifications. The historical line is not an archived snapshot for each year: revisions to today's list can change the reconstructed past, and inscription counts are not visitor numbers.

subgroups.name: Global Tourism Comparison
subgroups.title: 🌍 India vs the World's Top Destinations
subgroups.description: International arrivals, tourism receipts, spending per visitor and the tourism balance for India against France, Spain, the United States, China, Italy, Türkiye, Mexico, Thailand, Germany, the UK, Japan and the UAE.

categories.name: Sports
categories.title: 🏅 Sports: Medals, Wins & Records
categories.description: India's medals at the Olympics, Paralympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games, Games by Games and sport by sport, and the results and rankings of India's athletes, shooters, archers, wrestlers, boxers, lifters, shuttlers, tennis players, chess players and kabaddi teams, all taken from the official governing bodies.

subgroups.name: Olympic & Paralympic Medals
subgroups.title: 🥇 Olympic & Paralympic Medals
subgroups.description: Every medal India has won at the Summer Olympics (41) and Summer Paralympics (60), Games by Games and sport by sport, plus a cross-event view of medals in every sport India has reached a podium in at the four major multi-sport Games.

subgroups.name: Asian & Commonwealth Games
subgroups.title: 🏟️ Asian & Commonwealth Games
subgroups.description: India's 863 Asian Games and 602 Commonwealth Games medals by edition and by sport, with its Commonwealth medal-table position over time. Totals run to the 2026 Games in Aichi–Nagoya and Glasgow.

subgroups.name: Racket Sports
subgroups.title: 🏸 Badminton & Tennis
subgroups.description: Indian medals at the BWF World Championships, current BWF world rankings by discipline, Thomas, Uber and Sudirman Cup finishes, and India's Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup ties won and lost by decade.

subgroups.name: Shooting & Archery
subgroups.title: 🎯 Shooting & Archery
subgroups.description: Medals won by Indian shooters at ISSF World Championships and World Cups (2022 onwards), and by Indian archers at World Archery Championships and World Cup stages and Finals.

subgroups.name: Combat & Strength
subgroups.title: 🤼 Wrestling, Boxing & Weightlifting
subgroups.description: India's medals at the senior World Wrestling Championships (2025–26), the men's and women's World Boxing Championships, and the IWF World Weightlifting Championships (total-lift medals).

subgroups.name: Athletics
subgroups.title: 🏃 Athletics
subgroups.description: India's medals at the World Athletics Championships and the World Athletics U20 Championships, edition by edition, as published by World Athletics. Olympic, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games athletics medals are in the Games subgroups.

subgroups.name: Chess & Kabaddi
subgroups.title: ♟️ Chess & Kabaddi
subgroups.description: India's top-rated players, titled-player count and federation rank from the FIDE rating lists, Chess Olympiad match records, and the Pro Kabaddi League season standings.

categories.name: Cricket
categories.title: 🏏 Cricket: Wins, Losses, Rankings & Players
categories.description: All-time international results of India's men's and women's teams in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, records and titles at ICC tournaments, India's place in the official ICC team and player rankings, and career batting and bowling records that set today's players beside the greats.

subgroups.name: Men's Cricket
subgroups.title: 🏏 Men's Cricket
subgroups.description: All-time results of India's men's team in Tests, ODIs and T20Is: matches won, lost, drawn, tied and with no result, and win percentages by format.

subgroups.name: Women's Cricket
subgroups.title: 🏏 Women's Cricket
subgroups.description: All-time results of India's women's team across Tests, ODIs and T20Is.

subgroups.name: ICC Rankings
subgroups.title: 📈 ICC Team & Player Rankings
subgroups.description: India's position and rating in the official ICC team rankings for Tests, ODIs and T20Is, men and women, and the Indian batters, bowlers and all-rounders in the ICC player rankings.

subgroups.name: ICC Tournaments
subgroups.title: 🏆 ICC Tournaments
subgroups.description: India's match records at the men's and women's ODI World Cups, T20 World Cups and the Champions Trophy, edition by edition.

subgroups.name: Batting: Past vs Current
subgroups.title: 🏏 Batting: Past vs Current
subgroups.description: India's leading run-scorers in Tests, ODIs and T20Is, men and women, with career runs and batting averages. Every player is marked as past (retired) or current, so today's batters can be measured against the greats.

subgroups.name: Bowling: Past vs Current
subgroups.title: 🎯 Bowling: Past vs Current
subgroups.description: India's leading wicket-takers in every format, men and women, with career wickets and bowling averages, marking which bowlers are still playing and which are legends of earlier eras.

categories.name: Hockey
categories.title: 🏑 Hockey: Results, Rankings & Players
categories.description: Won, drawn and lost records of India's men's and women's hockey teams at the Olympics, World Cups and other FIH events, India's place in the current FIH world rankings, their FIH Hockey Pro League seasons, and goal-scoring and appearance records of past and current players.

subgroups.name: FIH Rankings & Pro League
subgroups.title: 📈 FIH Rankings & Pro League
subgroups.description: India's men's and women's FIH world-ranking points against the current top ten, and their standings in each FIH Hockey Pro League season.

subgroups.name: Men's Hockey
subgroups.title: 🏑 Men's Hockey
subgroups.description: Won, drawn and lost records of India's men's hockey team at the Olympics, the FIH World Cup and other FIH events, with goals scored and conceded.

subgroups.name: Women's Hockey
subgroups.title: 🏑 Women's Hockey
subgroups.description: Won, drawn and lost records of India's women's hockey team at the Olympics, the FIH World Cup and other FIH events.

subgroups.name: Hockey Players: Past vs Current
subgroups.title: 🏑 Hockey Players: Past vs Current
subgroups.description: Goals and appearances of India's men's and women's hockey players in official FIH-recorded matches, with each player marked as current or past.

categories.name: Football
categories.title: ⚽ Football: Results, Rankings & Players
categories.description: India's men's and women's national teams: FIFA ranking history, results by competition and year as recorded by FIFA, and the goals and appearances of past and current India internationals.

subgroups.name: FIFA Rankings
subgroups.title: 📈 FIFA Rankings
subgroups.description: India's men's and women's FIFA world ranking over the years, with the best and worst positions in each year, and India's place among Asian nations in the latest table.

subgroups.name: Men's Football
subgroups.title: ⚽ Men's Football
subgroups.description: India men's international results by competition and by year as recorded by FIFA: matches won, drawn and lost, with goals scored and conceded.

subgroups.name: Women's Football
subgroups.title: ⚽ Women's Football
subgroups.description: India women's international results by competition and by year as recorded by FIFA.

subgroups.name: Footballers: Past vs Current
subgroups.title: ⚽ Footballers: Past vs Current
subgroups.description: Goals and appearances of India men's international footballers in FIFA-recorded matches, marking which players are still in the national team and which have moved on.

categories.name: Innovation & Technology
categories.title: 💡 Innovation & Technology
categories.description: How fast India is inventing: patent and trademark filings by residents and non-residents, industrial designs, R&D spending and researchers, scientific publications, high-tech exports, IP royalty flows, digital adoption, new business formation and India's standing against other major economies.

subgroups.name: Patents & Intellectual Property
subgroups.title: 📜 Patents & Intellectual Property

indicators.title: Real GDP growth
indicators.subtitle: Annual real GDP growth
indicators.details:
Annual percentage growth in real gross domestic product. This is a historical national-accounts series, not a forecast.

Sourced from the World Bank indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.

indicators.title: CPI inflation
indicators.subtitle: Consumer prices
indicators.details:
Consumer price inflation tracks the annual change in the cost of a representative basket of goods and services. It is a broad measure of household purchasing-power pressure.

The series is useful alongside growth, exchange-rate, and trade indicators because imported costs and domestic demand can move inflation in different directions. Values are annual and come through the World Bank open API.

indicators.title: Per capita Net National Income
indicators.subtitle: Per capita NNI at current prices in Indian Rupees
indicators.details:
Per capita Net National Income (NNI) measures national income divided by population in current Indian Rupees. It expanded from ₹63,462 in FY2012 to ₹2.18 Lakh in FY2026.

Sourced from MOSPI National Accounts Statistics and official Economic Survey statements.

series.source: MOSPI National Accounts Statistics & Economic Survey (Per Capita Net National Income - NNI at Current Prices in INR)

indicators.title: Per capita GNI in PPP dollars
indicators.subtitle: GNI per capita in Purchasing Power Parity current international $
indicators.details:
GNI per capita converted to international dollars using purchasing power parity (PPP) rates, accounting for domestic price differences.

Sourced from World Bank Open Data indicator NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD.

datasets.label: Per capita GNI in PPP dollars

series.source: World Bank Open Data NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD (GNI per capita, PPP in current international $)

indicators.title: GST collections
indicators.subtitle: Gross monthly GST revenue
indicators.details:
GST collections are a high-frequency signal of recorded consumption and production moving through India's indirect-tax system. Strong receipts can reflect higher activity, improved compliance, price effects, or a combination of these factors.

The monthly series is collated from the Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.1. It should not be confused with a forecast or an estimate.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Fiscal deficit
indicators.subtitle: Union fiscal deficit as share of GDP
indicators.details:
The fiscal deficit is the gap between government expenditure and receipts excluding borrowings. It indicates how much the public sector needs to finance during a fiscal year.

The annual series is collated from official Economic Survey table 2.4 Excel files across previous editions and reported as a share of GDP.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 2.4; fiscal deficit as percent of GDP

indicators.title: IIP growth
indicators.subtitle: Industrial production
indicators.details:
Industrial production measures activity across mining, manufacturing, and electricity. It is a useful complement to GDP because it responds more directly to changes in factory output and infrastructure-linked production.

The monthly General IIP index is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.2; MOSPI remains the authoritative Indian source.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Rupee exchange rate
indicators.subtitle: INR per US dollar
indicators.details:
This series expresses the Indian rupee required to purchase one US dollar. A rising value means rupee depreciation against the dollar, all else equal.

Monthly exchange-rate observations are collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.4, with RBI DBIE linked as the official portal.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Trade share of GDP
indicators.subtitle: Exports plus imports as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Trade openness compares the combined value of exports and imports with GDP. It gives context for how strongly India's output is connected to external demand, imported inputs, and global price movements.

This is a ratio rather than a rupee total, so it can rise because trade grows or because GDP changes. The series is sourced through the World Bank open API.

indicators.title: Foreign exchange reserves
indicators.subtitle: Total reserves including gold
indicators.details:
Foreign-exchange reserves are external assets held by the monetary authority, including gold in this indicator. They help provide resilience against external-payment stress and exchange-rate volatility.

Reserve adequacy should be read with imports, debt, and the current account rather than treated as a standalone score. The displayed series is annual and denominated in current US dollars.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Bank credit
indicators.subtitle: Domestic credit to private sector
indicators.details:
Domestic credit to the private sector measures financial-sector lending relative to the size of the economy. It can signal whether businesses and households have expanding or tightening access to finance.

Credit growth is not automatically positive: the composition, repayment quality, and cost of borrowing matter. This annual ratio is a structural indicator, not a substitute for RBI monthly banking statistics.

indicators.title: Eight-core industries
indicators.subtitle: Core industrial production index
indicators.details:
The eight-core industries index tracks major infrastructure-linked sectors including coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery products, fertilisers, steel, cement, and electricity.

It is an important industrial activity companion to IIP and is collated from Economic Survey table 9.2.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Indian crude oil basket
indicators.subtitle: Average crude oil price
indicators.details:
The Indian crude oil basket price tracks an indicative average of crude prices relevant to India's import exposure. It helps explain fuel-cost pressure, inflation risk, and the external trade bill.

This is a crude price indicator, not a retail petrol or diesel price index. It is collated from Economic Survey table 9.3.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Fuel consumption
indicators.subtitle: Petroleum product consumption
indicators.details:
Fuel consumption measures petroleum product demand and is a useful activity proxy for transport, industry, and household energy use.

It is not a fuel price index. The dashboard labels it explicitly as consumption and sources it from Economic Survey table 9.4.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise exports
indicators.subtitle: Goods exports
indicators.details:
Merchandise exports measure the value of goods sold abroad. They connect the dashboard to external demand, foreign exchange earnings, and manufacturing competitiveness.

The monthly values are collated from Economic Survey table 9.4 and should be interpreted with imports and the current account.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise imports
indicators.subtitle: Goods imports
indicators.details:
Merchandise imports measure the value of goods purchased from abroad. They capture domestic demand, imported inputs, energy exposure, and pressure on the trade balance.

The monthly values are collated from Economic Survey table 9.4 and are not the same as total services-inclusive imports.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise trade balance
indicators.subtitle: Goods exports minus goods imports
indicators.details:
The monthly merchandise trade balance is calculated as goods exports minus goods imports. Positive values indicate a surplus and negative values a deficit.

This national total excludes services and does not identify balances with individual countries or regions.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.4; calculated as merchandise exports minus merchandise imports (national balance, not partner-specific)

indicators.title: Merchandise balance by trading partner
indicators.subtitle: Exports minus imports for leading partners
indicators.details:
This chart compares India's reported merchandise exports and imports with its leading trading partners for the latest year with matching observations. Positive values indicate a surplus; negative values indicate a deficit.

UN Comtrade reports exports on an FOB basis and imports on a CIF basis, so values are not perfectly symmetric. The chart covers goods only, not services, and is limited to the leading partners with verified code mappings.

series.source: UN Comtrade API, India merchandise trade by partner (2025); exports FOB minus imports CIF, top partners by trade value

indicators.title: GDP per capita
indicators.subtitle: Current US dollars per person
indicators.details:
GDP per capita divides the value of economic output by population. It is a broad scale indicator for comparing the economy over time, but it does not describe inequality, household income, or quality of life by itself.

The current-dollar series is sensitive to exchange rates and inflation. Read it alongside real growth and purchasing-power measures for a more complete picture.

indicators.title: Current account balance
indicators.subtitle: Balance as share of GDP
indicators.details:
The current account records trade in goods and services, income flows, and transfers with the rest of the world. A deficit means the country is spending more foreign exchange on these flows than it receives during the period.

This indicator connects directly to reserves, the rupee, and external financing conditions. It is shown as a share of GDP to make changes in national scale easier to compare.

indicators.title: Broad money
indicators.subtitle: Money supply as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Broad money captures currency and deposits available across the financial system. Relative to GDP, it provides a long-run view of liquidity and financial deepening.

It is not a direct measure of inflation or spending. Credit conditions, velocity, policy rates, and the distribution of deposits all influence how money supply affects the economy.

indicators.title: Tax revenue
indicators.subtitle: Tax revenue as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Tax revenue shows how much public revenue is collected through taxes relative to the size of the economy. It helps put fiscal capacity and public-service financing in a longer-run context.

The ratio can change because collections move, GDP moves, or both. It does not identify tax burden distribution or distinguish every type of levy.

indicators.title: Government consumption
indicators.subtitle: General government final consumption
indicators.details:
Government final consumption measures public-sector spending on goods and services relative to GDP. It is a useful context signal for the size of direct government demand in the economy.

This is not the same as the fiscal deficit: transfers, capital spending, receipts, and borrowing are treated differently in national accounts.

indicators.title: Foreign direct investment
indicators.subtitle: Net FDI inflows as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Foreign direct investment captures net cross-border investment intended to establish a lasting interest in an enterprise. Relative to GDP, it shows how important foreign investment flows are compared with national output.

A single year can be volatile because of large transactions, restructurings, or exceptional deals. It should be read with the current account and reserves.

indicators.title: Domestic savings
indicators.subtitle: Gross domestic savings as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Gross domestic savings is the portion of national output not used for final consumption. It provides a macro view of the resources potentially available for domestic investment.

The indicator does not show which households, firms, or public institutions save, nor whether savings are invested productively. Its value is strongest when compared with investment and external financing.

indicators.title: Indian Matrix publication cadence
indicators.subtitle: Articles published per week
indicators.details:
This graph tracks the public publication cadence of Indian Matrix articles. It adds the Substack source as a transparent, updateable public-data signal rather than treating article frequency as an economic or crime statistic.

The weekly RSS snapshot is collected by the pipeline and linked to Indian Matrix with appreciation for its visual public-data work.

indicators.title: Indian market indices
indicators.subtitle: Sensex, Nifty, and Nifty VIX; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This combined graph compares India's major equity-market indices and volatility using one normalized base-100 view. It makes direction and relative movement readable despite the different scales of the Sensex, Nifty, and VIX.

The monthly observations are collated from Economic Survey table 9.3. This is a market-context dashboard, not investment advice, and rebasing means the plotted values are relative rather than index levels.

series.source: BSE and NSE index histories, rebased to 100

indicators.title: Global equity market comparison
indicators.subtitle: BSE Sensex vs S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, and Shanghai Composite; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This graph compares India's primary equity benchmark (BSE Sensex) against leading global market indices (S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, Shanghai Composite) rebased to 100.

It illustrates the long-run compounding and relative performance of Indian capital markets alongside the world's major financial hubs.

series.source: BSE India, S&P Dow Jones, FTSE Russell, Nikkei Inc., SSE; Base 100 = 2000

indicators.title: World top economies GDP comparison
indicators.subtitle: GDP trajectories of India, US, China, Germany, Japan, and UK
indicators.details:
This chart plots the gross domestic product of India alongside the world's largest economies (United States, China, Germany, Japan, and United Kingdom) in current US dollars.

It contextualizes India's rise from an emerging developing economy following independence to one of the world's top 5 economic powerhouses.

series.source: World Bank API NY.GDP.MKTP.CD (GDP in current USD Trillion)

indicators.title: India sectoral market engines
indicators.subtitle: Nifty IT, Nifty Bank, Nifty Auto, Nifty Energy, and Sensex; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This series tracks key sectoral engines of India's stock market expansion—Technology, Banking & Financials, Automotive, and Energy—rebased to 100 alongside the benchmark Sensex.

It reveals how different industry pillars have spearheaded growth across economic cycles.

indicators.title: Global inflation benchmark comparison
indicators.subtitle: Consumer price inflation in India, US, and Euro Area
indicators.details:
This indicator compares consumer price inflation rate trends across India, the United States, and the Euro Area.

Reading India's inflation alongside major global central bank economies highlights how global commodity shocks, monetary policy, and exchange rates impact domestic price stability.

series.source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (Annual CPI inflation %)

indicators.title: Union Budget total expenditure
indicators.subtitle: Union budget total spending trajectory
indicators.details:
Total central government expenditure from post-independence budgets to modern Union Budgets in ₹ Lakh Crores.

Sourced from official Union Budget Expenditure statements.

series.source: Union Budget Documents, Ministry of Finance (Total Central Expenditure in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Union Budget YoY growth
indicators.subtitle: Annual percentage increase in Union expenditure
indicators.details:
Year-on-year percentage increase in central budget allocation.

Reflects fiscal policy expansion across economic cycles.

series.source: Union Budget of India, Ministry of Finance (Annual Central Expenditure YoY Growth %)

indicators.title: Union capital expenditure (Capex)
indicators.subtitle: Central budget capital expenditure for asset creation
indicators.details:
Capital Expenditure (Capex) allocation for roads, railways, ports, defense, and infrastructure creation.

Highlights India's strategic pivot toward asset building and long-term capital formation.

series.source: Ministry of Finance Budget Statements (Central Government Capital Outlay / Capex in INR Lakh Crores)

indicators.title: Gross tax revenue YoY growth
indicators.subtitle: Annual percentage growth in gross central tax collections
indicators.details:
Year-on-year growth rate of Gross Central Tax Collections.

Reflects tax compliance, economic activity, and fiscal revenue buoyancy. Sourced from Controller General of Accounts (CGA).

series.source: Controller General of Accounts (CGA) & Union Budget (Gross Central Tax Revenue Annual YoY Growth %)

indicators.title: Automobile production
indicators.subtitle: Total vehicles manufactured
indicators.details:
Total automobile manufacturing volume across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, and two-wheelers.

series.source: Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) (Total Automobile Production Output in Million Units)

indicators.title: Automobile domestic sales
indicators.subtitle: Annual sales by vehicle category, FY2008-09 to FY2013-14
indicators.details:
Annual domestic sales of passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, and two-wheelers as reported by SIAM. The headline series is total domestic sales, with category trends shown as separate chart lines.

SIAM's public table currently covers FY2008-09 through FY2013-14 only. This chart does not extrapolate the data or substitute production/registrations for sales.

series.source: SIAM Automobile Domestic Sales Trends (FY2008-09 to FY2013-14); annual domestic sales by vehicle category, million units

indicators.title: Real household consumption per capita
indicators.subtitle: Household final consumption per person, constant 2015 US dollars
indicators.details:
Households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs) final consumption expenditure per capita, expressed in constant 2015 US dollars. It provides a long-run, inflation-adjusted signal of material consumption per person.

It is an average, not a measure of distribution or each household's purchasing power, and it does not capture unpaid work or public services. Sourced from World Bank indicator NE.CON.PRVT.PC.KD.

indicators.title: ICT Service Exports
indicators.subtitle: Computer, communications and other services, % of service exports
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of India's service exports that come from IT, software, communications and related business services.

How to read it — A high, rising share shows how central the IT and global-capability-centre industry is to India's exports.

Why it matters — Services exports pay for much of India's merchandise trade deficit, making this sector a pillar of external stability.

series.note: Computer, communications and other services, % of service exports. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Gross Capital Formation
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross capital formation is the share of GDP spent on new fixed assets and inventory build-up. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 34.6% in 2025. A higher share means the economy is channelling more output into future capacity.

Why it matters — Investment is the engine of medium-term growth; India's rate shows how much of its growth is capital-led.

series.note: Gross Capital Formation: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 34.6%. Source: World Bank API NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Gross Capital Formation: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross capital formation is the share of GDP spent on new fixed assets and inventory build-up. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. A higher share means the economy is channelling more output into future capacity.

Why it matters — Investment is the engine of medium-term growth; India's rate shows how much of its growth is capital-led.

series.note: Gross Capital Formation: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Gross Capital Formation: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross capital formation is the share of GDP spent on new fixed assets and inventory build-up. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 1 of 12 (1 = highest value). A higher share means the economy is channelling more output into future capacity.

Why it matters — Investment is the engine of medium-term growth; India's rate shows how much of its growth is capital-led.

series.note: Gross Capital Formation, 2025: India ranks 1 of 12 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: GNI per Capita (PPP)
indicators.subtitle: India, 1990-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross national income per person converted at purchasing-power-parity so prices are comparable across countries. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 11,600 int. $ in 2025. Higher means more income per resident after adjusting for local price levels.

Why it matters — PPP income shows real living standards better than market exchange rates do.

series.note: GNI per Capita (PPP): India's annual series, 1990 to 2025; the latest value is 11,600 int. $. Source: World Bank API NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: GNI per Capita (PPP): Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross national income per person converted at purchasing-power-parity so prices are comparable across countries. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 12 of 15 (1 = highest value). Higher means more income per resident after adjusting for local price levels.

Why it matters — PPP income shows real living standards better than market exchange rates do.

series.note: GNI per Capita (PPP), 2025: India ranks 12 of 15 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Gross Savings Rate: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross savings is national income left after household and government consumption, as a share of GDP. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Lines above India mean peers save more of their income.

Why it matters — High domestic savings let a country fund investment without relying on foreign capital.

series.note: Gross Savings Rate: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: External Balance on Goods & Services
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — The external balance is exports minus imports of goods and services as a share of GDP. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at -1.74% in 2025. Values below zero are trade deficits; above zero are surpluses.

Why it matters — A persistent deficit must be financed by foreign inflows, so it signals external vulnerability.

series.note: External Balance on Goods & Services: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is -1.74%. Source: World Bank API NE.RSB.GNFS.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: External Balance on Goods & Services: Decade Averages
indicators.subtitle: India, average per decade
indicators.details:
What it shows — The external balance is exports minus imports of goods and services as a share of GDP. Annual values are averaged within each decade to smooth year-to-year noise.

How to read it — Compare bars left to right: the 2020s average is -1.8% against -1.95% in the 1980s. Values below zero are trade deficits; above zero are surpluses.

Why it matters — A persistent deficit must be financed by foreign inflows, so it signals external vulnerability.

datasets.label: External Balance on Goods & Services: Decade Averages

series.note: External Balance on Goods & Services: decade averages for India; the 2020s average is 0.15% above the 1980s. Source: World Bank API NE.RSB.GNFS.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100)
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — The consumer price index tracks the cost of a typical household basket, rebased so 2010 equals 100. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 233.06 index in 2025. A steeper line means faster cumulative price rises since the 2010 base.

Why it matters — The index level shows how much purchasing power has been eroded over the long run.

series.note: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100): India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 233.06 index. Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100): Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — The consumer price index tracks the cost of a typical household basket, rebased so 2010 equals 100. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 7 of 14 (1 = highest value). A steeper line means faster cumulative price rises since the 2010 base.

Why it matters — The index level shows how much purchasing power has been eroded over the long run.

series.note: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100), 2025: India ranks 7 of 14 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Consumer Price Inflation: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual percentage change in consumer prices. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Spikes show inflation episodes; a line near zero or below shows stable or falling prices.

Why it matters — Inflation decides real incomes, interest rates and central-bank policy.

series.note: Consumer Price Inflation: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Consumer Price Inflation: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual percentage change in consumer prices. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 9 of 14 (1 = highest value). Spikes show inflation episodes; a line near zero or below shows stable or falling prices.

Why it matters — Inflation decides real incomes, interest rates and central-bank policy.

series.note: Consumer Price Inflation, 2025: India ranks 9 of 14 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Consumer Price Inflation: Decade Averages
indicators.subtitle: India, average per decade
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual percentage change in consumer prices. Annual values are averaged within each decade to smooth year-to-year noise.

How to read it — Compare bars left to right: the 2020s average is 5.24% against 9.21% in the 1980s. Spikes show inflation episodes; a line near zero or below shows stable or falling prices.

Why it matters — Inflation decides real incomes, interest rates and central-bank policy.

series.note: Consumer Price Inflation: decade averages for India; the 2020s average is -3.97% below the 1980s. Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: PPP Conversion Factor
indicators.subtitle: India, 1990-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — How many rupees are needed to buy what one international dollar buys in the United States. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 20.09 LCU per int. $ in 2025. A rising line means the rupee's domestic purchasing power is falling relative to the dollar's.

Why it matters — It is the basis for converting India's GDP into internationally comparable PPP terms.

series.note: PPP Conversion Factor: India's annual series, 1990 to 2025; the latest value is 20.09 LCU per int. $. Source: World Bank API PA.NUS.PPP (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Comparative Price Level of Consumption: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Private-consumption PPP divided by the market exchange rate; values below 1 mean prices are lower than in the US. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Lower bars mean everyday goods and services are cheaper in dollar terms.

Why it matters — A low price level helps household affordability but also depresses dollar-measured GDP.

series.note: Comparative Price Level of Consumption: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, PA.NUS.FCRF (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Comparative Price Level of Consumption: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Private-consumption PPP divided by the market exchange rate; values below 1 mean prices are lower than in the US. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 14 of 15 (1 = highest value). Lower bars mean everyday goods and services are cheaper in dollar terms.

Why it matters — A low price level helps household affordability but also depresses dollar-measured GDP.

datasets.label: Comparative Price Level of Consumption: Peer Ranking (2025)

series.note: Comparative Price Level of Consumption, 2025: India ranks 14 of 15 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, PA.NUS.FCRF (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Broad Money Growth
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2021
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual growth in broad money (M3), the stock of currency, deposits and near-money. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 11.3% in 2021. Faster growth than GDP often precedes higher inflation or credit booms.

Why it matters — Money supply growth is a leading indicator for inflation and financial-sector expansion.

series.note: Broad Money Growth: India's annual series, 1980 to 2021; the latest value is 11.3%. Source: World Bank API FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2021.

indicators.title: Broad Money Growth: Decade Averages
indicators.subtitle: India, average per decade
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual growth in broad money (M3), the stock of currency, deposits and near-money. Annual values are averaged within each decade to smooth year-to-year noise.

How to read it — Compare bars left to right: the 2020s average is 11.89% against 17.06% in the 1980s. Faster growth than GDP often precedes higher inflation or credit booms.

Why it matters — Money supply growth is a leading indicator for inflation and financial-sector expansion.

series.note: Broad Money Growth: decade averages for India; the 2020s average is -5.17% below the 1980s. Source: World Bank API FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2021.

indicators.title: External Debt Stocks
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total external debt owed to non-residents as a share of gross national income. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 18.58% of GNI in 2024. Lower means the country's foreign obligations are small relative to its income.

Why it matters — A modest ratio protects against currency and rollover crises.

series.note: External Debt Stocks: India's annual series, 1980 to 2024; the latest value is 18.58% of GNI. Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: External Debt Stocks: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total external debt owed to non-residents as a share of gross national income. This chart overlays India with 3 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, Brazil, Bangladesh. Lower means the country's foreign obligations are small relative to its income.

Why it matters — A modest ratio protects against currency and rollover crises.

series.note: External Debt Stocks: India against 3 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: External Debt Stocks: Peer Ranking (2024)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total external debt owed to non-residents as a share of gross national income. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2024; India ranks 8 of 9 (1 = highest value). Lower means the country's foreign obligations are small relative to its income.

Why it matters — A modest ratio protects against currency and rollover crises.

series.note: External Debt Stocks, 2024: India ranks 8 of 9 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: External Debt Stock
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total outstanding external debt (public, publicly guaranteed and private) in US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 716.46 USD bn in 2024. The line shows how fast India's dollar obligations have grown.

Why it matters — The absolute stock matters because servicing it drains foreign-exchange reserves.

series.note: External Debt Stock: India's annual series, 1980 to 2024; the latest value is 716.46 USD bn. Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.CD (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Debt Service
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Principal plus interest paid on external debt as a share of exports of goods, services and income. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 10.49% of exports in 2024. A rising line means a bigger slice of export earnings is spent on debt.

Why it matters — Debt service relative to export earnings is a classic stress gauge for external solvency.

series.note: Debt Service: India's annual series, 1980 to 2024; the latest value is 10.49% of exports. Source: World Bank API DT.TDS.DECT.EX.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Debt Service: Decade Averages
indicators.subtitle: India, average per decade
indicators.details:
What it shows — Principal plus interest paid on external debt as a share of exports of goods, services and income. Annual values are averaged within each decade to smooth year-to-year noise.

How to read it — Compare bars left to right: the 2020s average is 10.36% of exports against 23.58% of exports in the 1980s. A rising line means a bigger slice of export earnings is spent on debt.

Why it matters — Debt service relative to export earnings is a classic stress gauge for external solvency.

series.note: Debt Service: decade averages for India; the 2020s average is -13.22% of exports below the 1980s. Source: World Bank API DT.TDS.DECT.EX.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Foreign-Exchange Reserves: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total reserves including gold held by the central bank, in US dollars. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 4 of 13 (1 = highest value). Bigger slices or bars mean a larger buffer for defending the currency and paying for imports.

Why it matters — Reserves are the first line of defence against capital-flow shocks.

series.note: Foreign-Exchange Reserves, 2025: India ranks 4 of 13 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API FI.RES.TOTL.CD (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Foreign-Exchange Reserves: Share Among Peers (2025)

indicators.details:

How to read it — Slices are shares of the group total in 2025; India holds 7.7% and ranks 4 of 13. A bigger slice means a larger absolute amount, not a better outcome.

Why it matters — Reserves are the first line of defence against capital-flow shocks.

series.note: Foreign-Exchange Reserves, 2025: India holds 7.7% of the group total and ranks 4 of 13. Source: World Bank API FI.RES.TOTL.CD (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.details:
What it shows — Personal transfers and compensation of employees sent home by workers abroad, in US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 150.71 USD bn in 2025. A rising line means more foreign income flowing to households.

Why it matters — India is the world's largest remittance recipient, a stable source of foreign currency.

series.note: Remittances Received: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 150.71 USD bn. Source: World Bank API BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 1 of 15 (1 = highest value). A rising line means more foreign income flowing to households.

Why it matters — India is the world's largest remittance recipient, a stable source of foreign currency.

series.note: Remittances Received, 2025: India ranks 1 of 15 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.subtitle: Each country's share of the 15-country total
indicators.details:
What it shows — Personal transfers and compensation of employees sent home by workers abroad, in US dollars. Slices show each country's share of the sampled countries' total.

How to read it — Slices are shares of the group total in 2025; India holds 38.6% and ranks 1 of 15. A bigger slice means a larger absolute amount, not a better outcome.

Why it matters — India is the world's largest remittance recipient, a stable source of foreign currency.

series.note: Remittances Received, 2025: India holds 38.6% of the group total and ranks 1 of 15. Source: World Bank API BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: WPI inflation
indicators.subtitle: Wholesale price inflation
indicators.details:
Wholesale price inflation tracks price movement at the producer and bulk-trade level. It can reveal input-cost pressure before those changes fully appear in consumer prices.

WPI is not included in the Economic Survey monthly HFI tables used by this pipeline. The Office of the Economic Adviser remains the official source, but its public portal does not currently expose a stable automated export for this dashboard.

series.source: Office of Economic Adviser WPI monthly workbook

indicators.title: Power consumption
indicators.subtitle: Electricity demand
indicators.details:
Power consumption is a high-frequency activity signal that reflects demand from households, services, and industry. It can move with weather, economic activity, and electrification.

The monthly series is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.1. It measures electricity use, not generation capacity or reliability.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: E-way bills
indicators.subtitle: Goods movement compliance volume
indicators.details:
E-way bills track electronically documented movement of goods. They provide a useful logistics and formal-commerce signal that complements GST collections.

The series is a transaction volume, not a rupee value or direct GDP estimate. It is collated from Economic Survey table 9.1.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Rail freight traffic
indicators.subtitle: Domestic rail freight
indicators.details:
Rail freight traffic reflects movement of bulk commodities and industrial inputs through the rail network. It provides a physical-economy signal alongside digital and tax indicators.

The series is reported in thousand tonnes and comes from Economic Survey table 9.1.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Port cargo traffic
indicators.subtitle: Cargo handled at ports
indicators.details:
Port cargo traffic captures goods handled through India's ports and gives context for external trade and domestic supply chains.

indicators.title: Registered Motor Vehicles
indicators.subtitle: Vehicles on record, transport vs non-transport (MoRTH)
indicators.details:
What it shows — The total stock of registered motor vehicles, split into private (non-transport: two-wheelers and cars) and commercial (transport: buses, trucks, taxis).

How to read it — Bars show the fleet on record; private vehicles make up the overwhelming majority.

Why it matters — Vehicle numbers drive fuel demand, urban congestion and air pollution, and set the scale of the EV transition.

series.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 112 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Values for 2021, 2022 are marked provisional by the source. National totals are the sum of State/UT registrations; the latest years are provisional.

indicators.title: India: Sector Composition of Value Added (2025)
indicators.subtitle: India, shares of total, 2025
indicators.source_url: World Bank API NV.AGR.TOTL.CD, NV.IND.TOTL.CD, NV.SRV.TOTL.CD
indicators.details:
What it shows — India's value added split across agriculture, industry (including construction and mining) and services.

How to read it — Larger slices dominate output; services typically lead as an economy matures. In 2025, Services is the largest slice at 54.4%.

Why it matters — The split shows how far India's structural transformation has progressed.

datasets.label: India: Sector Composition of Value Added (2025)

series.note: India: Sector Composition of Value Added, 2025: Services is the largest slice at 54.4%. Source: World Bank API NV.AGR.TOTL.CD, NV.IND.TOTL.CD, NV.SRV.TOTL.CD (World Bank national accounts / ILO); latest year with data: 2025.
